chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a deceased person over whom salat had been performed; then when the Imam gave salām, the deceased was found to be reversed, with his feet toward the place of his head. He said:

He is to be straightened, and the salat is to be repeated over him, even if he has already been carried away, so long as he has not been buried. But if he has been buried, then the salat over him has passed, and no salat is performed over him while he is buried.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the funeral salat performed over the deceased
key_terms.حُمِلَ: he was carried away from the place of prayer
key_terms.مَضَتِ: it has already been completed and stands as done
key_terms.يُسَوَّى: he is to be set straight or corrected in position

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person was positioned incorrectly during funeral salat, should the salat be repeated after burial?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about funeral salat when it is discovered that the deceased had been placed incorrectly. The body should be corrected and the salat repeated as long as burial has not yet occurred; once burial has taken place, the previous salat stands and no salat is performed over the buried deceased.
